intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

experiences.name: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market), a covered indoor market where you can taste local cheeses, olives, cured meats, spices, and fresh produce alongside locals. A guided or self-guided walk through the stalls offers an authentic culinary immersion away from the heat.

experiences.name: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach
experiences.description: Visit the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni in the late afternoon and evening when temperatures drop. Swim in the crystal-clear waters of the Saronic Gulf, enjoy sunbeds, and watch the spectacular Athenian Riviera sunset. Easily accessible from central Athens and close to quality seafood restaurants.

experiences.name: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine
experiences.description: Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a local kitchen in the Plaka district, learning to prepare classic dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, and tzatziki from scratch. Classes run in the evening to avoid heat, and you enjoy your creations as dinner afterward.

experiences.name: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island
experiences.description: Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina in the late afternoon, avoiding peak heat. Swim at the calm, clear beaches near Aegina Town, try the island's famous pistachio products and fresh fish at a harbor taverna, and return by evening ferry. A full island experience within budget and close to Athens.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Grab a souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk to ease into Greek food culture.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros or tiropita (cheese pie) from a bakery near the airport or on arrival — under €3
meals.dinner: Souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk in Monastiraki — around €2.50–€3.50

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 14:50 arrival. Use the Metro Line 3 from the airport to Monastiraki for about €9 — cheapest and fastest option into the city center.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket (~€20) also covers several other archaeological sites in Athens — great value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (covered by the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, browse the colorful Monastiraki Flea Market for local crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Psiri neighborhood for dinner. Explore the lively tavernas and try mezedes (small shared plates). Walk along Ermou Street for evening people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Souvlaki plate with pita, tzatziki, and salad from a local taverna in Monastiraki — €6–€8
meals.dinner: Mezedes spread at a Psiri taverna — order a few small plates like taramosalata, dolmades, and grilled halloumi — €10–€14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy the €20 combined Acropolis ticket — it covers 7 sites and is valid for 5 days, saving money overall. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Piraeus port and catch an early ferry to the island of Aegina (about 1 hour, ~€8–€10 each way). Aegina is one of the closest and most affordable Saronic islands from Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or take a local bus to the stunning Temple of Aphaia, one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples. Then head to Agia Marina beach — a beautiful sandy beach with calm, clear water perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Piraeus by evening ferry and head back to Athens. Enjoy dinner near the port or back in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a café near the hostel — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or calamari at a simple taverna near Agia Marina beach — €10–€13
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus and a Greek salad at a Piraeus portside taverna — €10–€12

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance at the Piraeus port or online. First ferry to Aegina is usually around 7:00–8:00 AM. Bring sunscreen and a swimsuit — the beach is excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) — a vibrant, authentic local market with fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and cheeses. A fantastic sensory experience and very budget-friendly for snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Archaeological Museum (€12 entry) — one of the world's greatest collections of ancient Greek artifacts. Spend 2–3 hours exploring treasures including the Antikythera Mechanism and Mycenaean gold.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the bohemian Exarchia neighborhood for an authentic, non-touristy Athens experience. Browse independent bookshops and street art, then find a local ouzeri for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh bread, olives, and local cheese from the Central Market stalls — €3–€5
meals.lunch: Cheap and filling moussaka or pastitsio at a traditional eatery near the museum — €7–€9
meals.dinner: Ouzeri in Exarchia — order ouzo and a selection of mezedes like fried zucchini, fava dip, and grilled sardines — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: The Central Market is closed on Sundays. The National Archaeological Museum is free on the first Sunday of each month — check if this applies to your visit.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early KTEL bus from Athens (Kifissos Bus Terminal) to Nafplio in the Peloponnese — about 2.5 hours, ~€13. Check into a budget guesthouse in this charming coastal town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful old town with its Venetian architecture and narrow lanes. Climb the 999 steps up to the impressive Palamidi Fortress (€8 entry) for panoramic views over the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Nafplio waterfront promenade at sunset. Enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of this romantic town and dine at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee before the bus — €2
meals.lunch: Grilled lamb chops (paidakia) with village salad at a Nafplio taverna — €10–€13
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood pasta or grilled sea bream at a waterfront restaurant — €11–€14

day_by_day.notes: Book the KTEL bus ticket in advance if possible. Nafplio is a great base for exploring the Peloponnese. The Palamidi climb is steep — go in the morning or late afternoon to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short local bus or taxi (~€10) to the ancient site of Epidaurus. Visit the remarkably preserved ancient theater — one of the best acoustically perfect theaters in the world — and the Sanctuary of Asclepius (€12 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, scenic rocky beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Swim in the crystal-clear Argolic Gulf waters.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Nafplio's Syntagma Square in the evening. Try local street food and browse the small shops selling local products like olive oil and honey.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey at a café in Nafplio — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local bakery — tiropita, spanakopita, and a bottle of water — €4–€5
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek taverna dinner — stuffed tomatoes (gemista), tzatziki, and village bread — €9–€12

day_by_day.notes: Epidaurus hosts a famous summer festival with ancient drama performances — check if any shows coincide with your visit (tickets from €15). Arvanitia Beach has free entry and is very clean.

day_by_day.morning: Take the KTEL bus from Nafplio to Athens (Kifissos Terminal), then connect to the port of Piraeus. Catch a ferry to Hydra island (~2 hours from Piraeus, ~€18–€22 each way on a Flying Dolphin hydrofoil).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hydra town — a car-free island with stunning architecture, donkeys as transport, and crystal-clear waters. Walk along the harbor and up the hillside paths. Swim at Vlychos or Kamini beach, both reachable on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the magical sunset over Hydra harbor. Have dinner at a portside taverna before catching the last hydrofoil back to Piraeus and returning to Athens.

meals.breakfast: Cheese pie and coffee at the Nafplio bus station — €3
meals.lunch: Grilled fish of the day at a simple Hydra harbor taverna — €12–€15
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus and a cold Mythos beer at a portside spot in Hydra — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: Hydra is slightly pricier than other islands due to its exclusivity, but a day trip keeps costs manageable. Check the last hydrofoil return time carefully — usually around 7:00–8:00 PM. No motorized vehicles on Hydra.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Piraeus to Paros island (~4–5 hours by regular ferry, ~€30–€35, or faster by high-speed ferry). Check into a budget room or hostel in Parikia, the island's main town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Parikia's charming whitewashed old town (Kastro). Visit the beautiful Panagia Ekatontapiliani (Church of 100 Doors) — free entry. Relax at Livadia Beach, a sandy beach just a short walk from town.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through Parikia's narrow alleys as the sun sets. Enjoy the lively but relaxed island atmosphere and dine at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee before boarding the ferry in Piraeus — €3
meals.lunch: Fresh calamari and Greek salad at a Parikia waterfront taverna — €10–€13
meals.dinner: Grilled lamb souvlaki plate with tzatziki and pita at a local grill house — €8–€10

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets in advance during June as they fill up quickly. Paros is one of the best-value Cycladic islands. Budget accommodation in Parikia ranges from €20–€40/night for a dorm or simple room.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV (€15–€25/day) to explore Paros at your own pace. Head to the beautiful village of Naoussa in the north — a picturesque fishing village with a Venetian harbor.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Naoussa, visit Kolymbithres Beach — famous for its unique granite rock formations and turquoise water. Swim and snorkel in the clear Aegean Sea. Continue to Santa Maria Beach for more swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Parikia. Enjoy a sunset drink at a clifftop bar, then have dinner at a local fish taverna near the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Fresh orange juice and a bougatsa (custard pastry) at a Parikia bakery — €3–€4
meals.lunch: Grilled fresh fish and village salad at a simple Naoussa taverna — €12–€15
meals.dinner: Octopus stifado (stew) and a carafe of local house wine at a Parikia taverna — €11–€14

day_by_day.notes: Kolymbithres is one of the most photographed beaches in the Cyclades — arrive before noon to get a good spot. Scooter rental requires a valid license. Fuel up the scooter before returning.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short ferry from Paros to Naxos (~45 minutes, ~€8–€10) — the largest and most fertile Cycladic island. Check into budget accommodation in Naxos Town (Chora).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Naxos Town's impressive Venetian Kastro (castle) and the iconic Portara — a massive ancient marble doorway on a small islet connected to the harbor by a causeway. Free to visit and stunning at any time of day.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the atmospheric old town market streets. Sample local Naxian products — the island is famous for its potatoes, cheese (graviera), and citron liqueur (kitron). Dine at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and a cheese pie from a Paros bakery before the ferry — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Naxian graviera cheese and local bread with olives from a market stall — €4–€6
meals.dinner: Slow-cooked lamb with Naxian potatoes at a traditional Chora taverna — €10–€13

day_by_day.notes: Naxos is one of the best-value Cycladic islands with excellent local produce. The Portara is especially beautiful at sunset — plan to be there around 7:30–8:00 PM. Try a small glass of kitron liqueur — a unique local specialty.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local KTEL bus from Naxos Town to Agios Prokopios Beach — consistently rated one of Greece's best beaches with long stretches of fine white sand and shallow turquoise water. Spend the morning swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coast to Agia Anna Beach and Plaka Beach — quieter and more natural stretches of coastline. Bring snacks and water for a full beach afternoon. The bus runs regularly along this coastal route.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Naxos Town for the evening. Browse the old town's small shops selling local honey, olive oil, and ceramics. Enjoy a final Naxos dinner with fresh seafood.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with Naxian thyme honey and fresh fruit at a Chora café — €4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a bakery — spanakopita, fruit, and water — €4–€5 (eat on the beach)
meals.dinner: Grilled sea bass with lemon and olive oil, plus a village salad at a Naxos Town taverna — €12–€15

day_by_day.notes: Agios Prokopios and Plaka beaches have free access. Sun loungers are available for rent (~€5–€8 each) but bringing your own towel and lying on the sand is free. Apply sunscreen regularly — June sun is strong.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry back from Naxos to Piraeus (~5–6 hours by regular ferry, ~€35–€40). Enjoy the scenic Aegean crossing and relax on deck. Arrive in Athens by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Back in Athens, visit any remaining sites from the combined Acropolis ticket (valid 5 days) — such as the Ancient Agora, Kerameikos, or the Roman Agora. Alternatively, explore the Anafiotika neighborhood — a tiny Cycladic-style village hidden on the slopes of the Acropolis hill.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — head to the Thissio neighborhood for rooftop bar drinks with Acropolis views. Enjoy a farewell Greek dinner in the Plaka or Monastiraki area.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri and coffee at the Naxos port before boarding — €2–€3
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry — bring your own food or buy a simple sandwich on board — €4–€6
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Plaka taverna — moussaka, Greek salad, grilled halloumi, and a carafe of house wine — €14–€18

day_by_day.notes: Book the return ferry from Naxos in advance. The overnight or early morning ferry options are cheaper but the daytime crossing offers beautiful scenery. Anafiotika is a hidden gem — very few tourists find it.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Take a last walk through Monastiraki and pick up any remaining souvenirs — local olive oil, dried herbs, honey, or small ceramic pieces are affordable and authentic gifts. Visit a local café for a proper Greek breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Athens International Airport via Metro Line 3 from Monastiraki or Syntagma (~€9, ~40 minutes). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your departure flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with wonderful memories of beaches, ancient history, and incredible local food.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a Monastiraki café — eggs, feta, olives, tomatoes, and Greek coffee — €6–€8
meals.lunch: Final souvlaki wrap or gyros from a street kiosk near the Metro station — €3
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Keep €10–€15 in cash for the Metro to the airport and any last-minute expenses. Greek airports have a departure tax included in most ticket prices. Double-check your flight time and terminal. Καλό ταξίδι — Have a great journey!

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day – no morning activities scheduled. Flight lands at 14:50.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos), clear customs and collect luggage. Take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens (~40 min). Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll through Monastiraki Square and the surrounding streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Psiri neighborhood for your first taste of Athens nightlife and local food culture. Explore the lively tavernas and mezedopoleio (meze restaurants) along Miaouli and Agion Anargyron streets. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner with Greek wine.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport or a quick souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk near your hotel (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional taverna in Psiri – try grilled octopus, tzatziki, and horiatiki salad (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after the 14:50 arrival. Keep the evening light to recover from travel. Exchange some cash or use ATMs in the airport arrivals hall for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a classic Greek breakfast at a local café near your hotel – freddo espresso, tiropita (cheese pie), and fresh orange juice. Then visit the Acropolis early (open from 8:00 AM) to beat the midday heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and the stunning panoramic views over Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Acropolis Museum (€10 entry) to see the original sculptures and artifacts from the hill. Afterward, wander through the charming Plaka neighborhood – Athens' oldest district – browsing artisan shops and soaking in the neoclassical architecture. Stop at Hadrian's Arch and the Temple of Olympian Zeus nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Metro or a short taxi to Piraeus and enjoy the featured experience: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor. Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna sampling fresh grilled fish, shrimp saganaki, and local Assyrtiko white wine while watching the yachts in the picturesque harbor.

meals.breakfast: Local café near hotel – tiropita, freddo espresso (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Plaka – stuffed vine leaves, Greek salad, and pita at a shaded taverna (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor, Piraeus – fresh catch of the day, meze, and wine (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets online in advance to skip queues. Wear comfortable shoes with good grip for the marble pathways. Mikrolimano is about 30 min from central Athens by Metro (Line 1 to Piraeus, then short taxi).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street – a vibrant, authentic market with fresh fish, meat, spices, olives, and local produce. A fantastic sensory experience and great for picking up local snacks. Then explore the nearby Monastiraki Flea Market for vintage finds and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Metro to Glyfada (southern Athens Riviera) for your first beach afternoon of the trip. Glyfada Beach offers clean waters, sunbeds, and a relaxed atmosphere. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the 23°C Mediterranean warmth. The beach is easily accessible and has good facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens and dine in the Koukaki neighborhood – a local favorite with authentic, non-touristy restaurants. Try a mezedopoleio for a spread of small dishes shared at the table.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh bread, olives, and local cheese from the Central Market stalls (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar at Glyfada – grilled corn, fresh fruit, or a light sandwich (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Mezedopoleio in Koukaki – shared plates of taramosalata, grilled halloumi, loukaniko sausage, and local draft beer (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Riviera beaches are reachable by tram from Syntagma Square. Glyfada is about 45 min by tram. Bring sunscreen – UV index is high in June even at 23°C.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens early by ferry from Piraeus Port to Mykonos (approximately 4.5–5 hours by conventional ferry or 2.5 hours by high-speed). Book tickets in advance. Enjoy the sea crossing with coffee and a snack on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Mykonos Town (Chora). Check in to your mid-range hotel or guesthouse. Explore the iconic whitewashed alleys of Chora, visit the famous windmills at Kato Mili, and stroll along Little Venice waterfront. Browse the boutique shops and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Mykonos Town at a local taverna away from the main tourist strip – ask locals for recommendations. The area around the old port has more authentic and affordable options than the main square.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near Piraeus port before boarding (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Light meal on the ferry or grab a gyros wrap upon arrival in Mykonos Town (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek taverna in Mykonos Chora – fresh fish, Greek salad, and local wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets at least a week in advance in June – routes fill up quickly. High-speed ferries (SeaJets, Golden Star) are faster but pricier. Conventional ferries (Blue Star) are more budget-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short bus or taxi to Agios Sostis Beach – one of Mykonos' most beautiful and less commercialized beaches. Crystal-clear turquoise water, golden sand, and a relaxed vibe. Swim and snorkel in the calm morning waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Move on to Ornos Beach or Platis Gialos Beach (both accessible by bus) for more swimming and sunbathing. These beaches have good facilities, sunbed rentals, and beach bars. Enjoy the warm Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for sunset at Little Venice – one of the most iconic sunset spots in Greece. Watch the sun dip into the Aegean from a waterfront café. Then enjoy dinner at a local fish taverna near the old port.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery – spanakopita and Greek yogurt with honey (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Platis Gialos – grilled calamari, village salad, and cold Mythos beer (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Fish taverna near Mykonos old port – grilled sea bream, tzatziki, and house wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos public buses (KTEL) are affordable and connect most beaches. Buy a day pass for convenience. Agios Sostis has no facilities so bring water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short boat excursion to the sacred island of Delos (30 min from Mykonos Town, boats depart 9:00–10:00 AM). Explore one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece – the birthplace of Apollo and Artemis. Walk among ancient temples, mosaics, and the famous Terrace of the Lions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon at Elia Beach – the longest beach on the island, with calm waters and a more relaxed crowd. Rent a sunbed and enjoy the afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Mykonos Town's famous nightlife scene at your own pace. Start with cocktails at a rooftop bar, then enjoy a final dinner in Chora before an early night ahead of tomorrow's travel.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the Delos boat – Greek yogurt, honey, and walnuts at a café (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on Delos (no restaurants on the island) or quick bite upon return to Mykonos Town (€6–10)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Mykonos Chora – lamb chops, roasted vegetables, and local Cycladic wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Delos entry fee is €12. Boats depart from the old port and return by 3:00 PM. Bring water, a hat, and sunscreen – there is no shade on Delos. Book the boat ticket the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Mykonos accommodation. Take a high-speed ferry from Mykonos to Santorini (approximately 2–2.5 hours). Enjoy the scenic Aegean crossing. Arrive in Santorini (Athinios Port) and transfer to your hotel in Fira or Imerovigli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and settle into your Santorini accommodation. Take the cable car or walk the famous zigzag path up to Fira Town. Explore the main town – browse the clifftop shops, visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (€6), and enjoy the dramatic caldera views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a short bus to Oia village for the world-famous Santorini sunset. Arrive at least an hour early to secure a good viewing spot. After sunset, enjoy dinner in Oia or take the bus back to Fira for more affordable dining options.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at Mykonos port café before boarding (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Fira after check-in – gyros or a café sandwich with caldera views (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fira (more affordable than Oia) – moussaka, stuffed tomatoes, and local Vinsanto wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Santorini ferry tickets should be booked in advance. The cable car in Fira costs €6 one way. Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset in June – arrive by 7:00 PM for the best spots.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri – a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption of 1627 BC (entry €12). Often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Afterward, head to the nearby Red Beach – one of Santorini's most dramatic and unique beaches with striking red volcanic cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the island's southeastern coast – long black sand beaches with clear water, beach bars, and sunbed rentals. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on the distinctive volcanic black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira for dinner. Explore the caldera-side restaurants and bars. Try a local winery for a tasting of Santorini's unique Assyrtiko white wine before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery in Fira – tiropita, fresh juice, and coffee (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Perivolos – fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold beer (€15–20)
meals.dinner: Caldera-view restaurant in Fira – grilled octopus, fava dip (Santorini specialty), and Assyrtiko wine (€25–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach requires a short walk over rocky terrain – wear sturdy sandals. Buses connect Fira to Akrotiri and Perissa regularly. Santorini's fava (yellow split pea purée) is a local specialty not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Join a morning catamaran sailing tour around the Santorini caldera (typically 5–6 hours, €60–90 per person). Sail past the volcanic islands of Nea Kameni and Palea Kameni, swim in the hot springs, snorkel in crystal-clear waters, and enjoy a BBQ lunch on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: The catamaran tour typically returns by early-to-mid afternoon. Rest at your hotel or explore Imerovigli – a quieter clifftop village between Fira and Oia with stunning caldera views and fewer crowds than Oia.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely final evening in Santorini. Visit a local wine bar for a tasting of Nykteri and Vinsanto wines, then have a relaxed dinner in Fira.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before the early catamaran departure (€6–9 if not included)
meals.lunch: BBQ lunch included on the catamaran – grilled meats, salads, and drinks
meals.dinner: Wine bar and dinner in Fira – cheese platter, local sausages, and a glass of Vinsanto dessert wine (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran tour at least 2–3 days in advance through your hotel or a local agency. Bring a towel, sunscreen, and a light layer for the sea breeze. Tours typically depart from Vlychada or Ammoudi Bay.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Santorini accommodation. Take a ferry back to Athens (Piraeus) – approximately 5–8 hours by conventional ferry or 4.5 hours by high-speed. Enjoy the scenic return journey across the Aegean. Alternatively, take a short domestic flight (30 min) if budget allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Athens. Check in to your hotel. Take a relaxed afternoon walk through the Thissio neighborhood – a trendy area with café-lined streets and views of the Acropolis. Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (€10) if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in the Thissio or Gazi neighborhood – both are lively areas with excellent mid-range restaurants and a local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Santorini port café before boarding (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Ferry snack bar or packed food from a Santorini bakery (€6–10)
meals.dinner: Modern Greek cuisine restaurant in Gazi – creative takes on traditional dishes, local craft beer (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If taking the conventional ferry, book a comfortable seat or cabin for the longer journey. The Gazi neighborhood is Athens' creative hub with excellent food and a vibrant evening atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Cape Sounion (about 70 km from Athens). Join a guided tour or take the KTEL bus from Pedion Areos. Visit the magnificent Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60 meters above the sea – one of Greece's most dramatic ancient sites with sweeping Aegean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at one of the Athenian Riviera beaches – Vouliagmeni Lake (a natural thermal lake with mineral-rich waters, €8 entry) or Vouliagmeni Beach for a swim. The water is calm and clear along this stretch of coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens for a final evening in the city. Visit the Syntagma Square area to watch the Evzone guards at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, then enjoy dinner in the Kolonaki neighborhood – Athens' upscale but accessible dining district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or neighborhood café – Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, freddo cappuccino (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Taverna near Cape Sounion – fresh seafood and salad with a view (€15–20)
meals.dinner: Kolonaki restaurant – slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, roasted potatoes, and a carafe of house wine (€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses to Cape Sounion depart from Pedion Areos Park (near Areos Park Metro stop) roughly every hour. The round trip takes about 3 hours total travel time. Entry to the Temple of Poseidon is €10.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum of Athens (€12) – one of the world's great museums, housing treasures from across ancient Greece including the Antikythera Mechanism, Mycenaean gold masks, and stunning classical sculptures. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Benaki Museum (€9) or the Museum of Cycladic Art (€7) for more curated Greek cultural experiences. Afterward, take a final stroll through the Ermou Street shopping area and the Monastiraki neighborhood for last-minute souvenir shopping and browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a special farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Athens with Acropolis views – a memorable way to end the trip. Splurge slightly on this final dinner for a truly Greek experience.

meals.breakfast: Neighborhood café near hotel – spanakopita, Greek coffee, and fresh orange juice (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a family-run taverna in Exarchia neighborhood near the National Museum – daily specials, home-cooked style (€12–16)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant with Acropolis view in Monastiraki or Thissio – grilled lamb, mezedes spread, and Greek wine (€30–40 per person, a worthy splurge)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays – check the schedule. Book the rooftop farewell dinner in advance as these restaurants fill up quickly in June. Pack your bags tonight for an early departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café. Depending on your departure time, take a final walk through Monastiraki or sit at a café in Syntagma Square for one last Greek coffee and people-watching. Pick up any final souvenirs – local honey, olive oil, or Mastiha liqueur make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) via Metro Line 3 from Syntagma or Monastiraki (€9, approximately 40 min). Check in for your return Air Serbia flight. Browse the airport's duty-free for Greek products.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of Greek beaches, ancient history, island-hopping, and incredible local food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast – bougatsa (custard-filled pastry), Greek coffee, and fresh juice at a local café (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a final souvlaki wrap near the hotel before heading to the airport (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the Metro journey and airport check-in/security. Metro Line 3 runs directly to the airport from central Athens. Keep your transit card or buy a single airport ticket (€9). Ensure all souvenirs with liquids are in checked luggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor
experiences.description: Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus, sampling fresh grilled octopus, sea bream, and local mezedes. Evening dining avoids the heat and offers a romantic harbor atmosphere with local crowds rather than tourists.

experiences.name: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market), a covered indoor market where you can taste local cheeses, olives, cured meats, spices, and fresh produce alongside locals. A guided or self-guided walk through the stalls offers an authentic culinary immersion away from the heat.

experiences.name: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach
experiences.description: Visit the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni in the late afternoon and evening when temperatures drop. Swim in the crystal-clear waters of the Saronic Gulf, enjoy sunbeds, and watch the spectacular Athenian Riviera sunset. Easily accessible from central Athens and close to quality seafood restaurants.

experiences.name: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine
experiences.description: Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a local kitchen in the Plaka district, learning to prepare classic dishes such as moussaka, spanakopita, and tzatziki from scratch. Classes run in the evening to avoid heat, and you enjoy your creations as dinner afterward.

experiences.name: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island
experiences.description: Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina in the late afternoon, avoiding peak heat. Swim at the calm, clear beaches near Aegina Town, try the island's famous pistachio products and fresh fish at a harbor taverna, and return by evening ferry. A full island experience within budget and close to Athens.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your hotel in the Athens Riviera area. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the waterfront promenade to begin soaking in the Mediterranean atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Seafood Dinner at Mikrolimano Harbor — Dine at a traditional waterfront taverna in the charming Mikrolimano harbor area of Piraeus. Sample freshly caught seafood including grilled octopus, sea bream, and prawns saganaki while watching the yachts bob in the harbor under the warm June evening sky.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Light meal at Athens Airport arrivals hall — try the airport's premium lounge or a café
meals.dinner: Mikrolimano Harbor waterfront taverna — fresh seafood platter, local white wine (Assyrtiko), and mezedes

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Mikrolimano is approximately 20–30 minutes from the airport by car. Dress smart-casual for the harbor dinner. June evenings are warm (~18–20°C), perfect for outdoor dining.

day_by_day.morning: Indoor Athens Central Market Food Tour — Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market), a covered indoor market brimming with fresh fish, meats, spices, olives, and cheeses. A knowledgeable local guide will walk you through the stalls, share stories of Greek culinary traditions, and offer tastings of cured meats, local honey, and artisan cheeses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for a leisurely afternoon. Browse high-end boutiques and galleries, then visit the Benaki Museum for a curated look at Greek art and culture across the ages. Enjoy a coffee break at a chic Kolonaki café.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Cooking Class: Traditional Greek Cuisine — Join a small-group indoor evening cooking class in a local kitchen in the Plaka district. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as spanakopita, moussaka, and loukoumades under the guidance of a professional Greek chef. Enjoy the meal you've prepared with local wine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — opt for a full Greek spread with yogurt, thyme honey, fresh fruit, and pastries
meals.lunch: Mezedopoleio in Monastiraki — a premium meze restaurant with shared plates of taramosalata, grilled halloumi, and stuffed vine leaves
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner of dishes prepared during the cooking class, paired with Nemea red wine or Santorini white

day_by_day.notes: The Central Market tour is best experienced in the morning when the market is most lively. Book the cooking class in advance as spots fill quickly. Plaka is walkable from most central Athens hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Acropolis and Parthenon — Beat the midday heat and crowds with an early morning private tour. A licensed archaeologist guide will bring the history of ancient Athens to life. Follow with a visit to the state-of-the-art Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sunset Swimming at Vouliagmeni Beach — Transfer by private car to the upscale organized beach of Vouliagmeni in the late afternoon. Rent a premium sun lounger and umbrella, swim in the crystal-clear Saronic Gulf waters, and enjoy the beach bar's cocktail menu as the sun begins its descent.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a fine-dining restaurant in Vouliagmeni or Glyfada — enjoy contemporary Greek cuisine with panoramic sea views. Try dishes like sea bass carpaccio, lobster pasta, and pistachio baklava for dessert.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Greek yogurt parfait, smoked salmon, fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Acropolis Museum café with views of the Parthenon — salads, sandwiches, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Fine-dining seafood restaurant in Vouliagmeni — tasting menu with wine pairing featuring Greek varietals

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and private guide well in advance. Vouliagmeni Beach has an entrance fee and premium facilities. Bring reef-safe sunscreen. The beach is approximately 25 km from central Athens.

day_by_day.morning: Late morning departure by high-speed ferry from Piraeus port to Mykonos. Enjoy the scenic 2.5-hour journey across the Aegean Sea from the ferry's premium lounge deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Mykonos and check into a luxury boutique hotel in Mykonos Town (Chora). After settling in, explore the iconic whitewashed alleys of Chora, visit the famous windmills overlooking the sea, and browse the upscale jewelry and fashion boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Little Venice, Mykonos — dine with your feet practically over the Aegean Sea. Enjoy fresh lobster, grilled fish, and local Mykonian cheeses while watching the sunset paint the sky in shades of orange and pink.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — continental spread with local pastries and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Light mezedes and drinks on the ferry's premium deck, or a quick bite upon arrival in Mykonos Town
meals.dinner: Little Venice waterfront restaurant — lobster spaghetti, grilled whole fish, and local Mykonian kopanisti cheese with wine

day_by_day.notes: Book high-speed ferry tickets (e.g., Seajet or Golden Star Ferries) in advance. Mykonos is extremely popular in June — luxury hotel reservations should be made months ahead. Little Venice restaurants fill up fast; reserve a table for sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat charter around Mykonos — Depart from Mykonos port on a private luxury sailing yacht or speedboat. Visit secluded coves and sea caves, snorkel in turquoise waters, and stop at the pristine beaches of Agios Sostis and Panormos, accessible only by sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat trip to the sacred island of Delos — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece. Walk among ancient temples, mosaics, and the iconic Terrace of the Lions with your private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar in Chora, then head to a premium restaurant for dinner featuring Mykonian specialties.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict, fresh pastries, Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the yacht charter — local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, fruit, and chilled rosé wine served on deck
meals.dinner: Upscale Mykonian restaurant — slow-cooked lamb, fresh fish, and local loukoumades with honey and walnuts

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charters can be arranged through the hotel concierge. Delos has restricted visiting hours and no overnight stays are permitted. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Delos. Apply high-SPF sunscreen for the full day on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning at Psarou Beach — one of Mykonos's most exclusive beaches. Rent a premium VIP sunbed setup with table service. Swim in the calm, clear waters and enjoy the glamorous atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nammos Beach Club or a similar luxury beach club at Psarou for an indulgent afternoon of cocktails, light bites, and world-class DJ music. Alternatively, explore the quieter Elia Beach for a more relaxed premium beach experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Mykonos at a top-rated fine-dining restaurant — enjoy a chef's tasting menu showcasing the best of Cycladic cuisine, paired with an expertly curated Greek wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread including smoked salmon, avocado toast, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Psarou — grilled octopus, fresh salads, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Fine-dining tasting menu restaurant in Mykonos Town — 6-course meal with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Psarou Beach VIP sunbeds require advance reservation and have a minimum spend. June 21 is the summer solstice — the longest day of the year, making for a spectacular late sunset over the Aegean.

day_by_day.morning: Morning ferry or short flight from Mykonos to Santorini. Arrive and check into a luxury cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli with a private plunge pool and caldera views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the iconic village of Oia on foot — wander through the blue-domed churches, art galleries, and artisan shops. Visit the Oia Castle ruins for panoramic caldera views. Take a private wine tour at one of Santorini's prestigious wineries (e.g., Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas) to taste the island's unique volcanic Assyrtiko wines.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from Oia — one of the world's most celebrated sunsets. Secure a premium spot at a cliffside restaurant or your hotel's terrace. Follow with a romantic dinner at a caldera-view fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Mykonos hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Greek lunch at a local taverna in Fira or Oia upon arrival — fresh tomato salad, fava dip, and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Caldera-view fine-dining restaurant in Oia — tuna tartare, grilled sea bass, and Santorinian white eggplant dish with Assyrtiko wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The ferry from Mykonos to Santorini takes approximately 2–3 hours (high-speed). Alternatively, a 30-minute flight is available. Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset — your hotel terrace or a reserved restaurant table is the most comfortable option.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran cruise around Santorini — Sail along the caldera's dramatic volcanic cliffs, visit the hot springs near Nea Kameni volcanic island, and swim in the warm mineral-rich waters. Snorkel at the Red Beach and White Beach, two of Santorini's most striking geological formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the catamaran cruise with a stop at the secluded Mesa Pigadia beach. Enjoy a gourmet lunch on deck as you sail back toward Oia, taking in the dramatic caldera panorama from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest point — for a quieter, more authentic experience away from the tourist crowds. Enjoy dinner at a traditional taverna with panoramic island views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast on your private terrace — Greek yogurt, local honey, fresh fruit, and pastries with caldera views
meals.lunch: Gourmet catered lunch on the catamaran — fresh seafood, salads, local cheeses, and chilled Santorinian wine
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Pyrgos village — slow-roasted lamb, village salad, and local Vinsanto dessert wine

day_by_day.notes: Private catamaran charters typically depart from Vlychada or Ammoudi Bay. Book well in advance for June. Bring motion sickness medication if needed. The hot springs will stain light-colored swimwear — wear an older suit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement buried by a volcanic eruption around 1600 BC, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Explore with a private guide who will bring the ancient frescoes and city layout to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Perissa Black Sand Beach — relax on Santorini's famous volcanic black sand beach on the island's southeastern coast. The beach is lined with premium beach bars and restaurants. Swim in the clear blue Aegean waters and enjoy the dramatic backdrop of Mesa Vouno mountain.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at your hotel's infinity pool overlooking the caldera, followed by a premium dinner at one of Santorini's most acclaimed restaurants in Imerovigli or Oia.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Greek spread with local Santorinian products including cherry tomatoes, capers, and fava
meals.lunch: Premium beach restaurant at Perissa — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer or rosé
meals.dinner: Award-winning restaurant in Imerovigli — modern Greek tasting menu with caldera views and sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking. The site is partially covered, making it comfortable even in warm weather. Black sand at Perissa gets very hot in the afternoon sun — water shoes are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast on your hotel terrace, take a dip in your private plunge pool, and soak in the caldera views. Optional: sunrise yoga session arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island — Take a short ferry from Piraeus to the nearby island of Aegina in the late afternoon (note: return to Athens mainland first by ferry, then connect to Aegina, or arrange a private speedboat transfer). Alternatively, spend the afternoon exploring Fira, Santorini's capital, with its museums, boutiques, and cliff-edge cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by evening flight from Santorini (approximately 45 minutes). Check into a luxury hotel in central Athens or the Riviera. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — eggs any style, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and specialty Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Fira café — mezedes, fresh bread, and local wine
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Athens with Acropolis illumination views — grilled meats, fresh salads, and local craft beer or wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Santorini–Athens flight in advance (Aegean Airlines or Olympic Air). Evening flights from Santorini can be delayed in peak season — build in buffer time. The Acropolis is beautifully lit at night and visible from many central Athens rooftop restaurants.

day_by_day.morning: Late Afternoon Boat Trip to Aegina Island (rescheduled as a morning/midday excursion) — Take the high-speed ferry from Piraeus to Aegina (35 minutes). Visit the stunning Temple of Aphaia, one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples, with a private guide. Explore the charming Aegina Town harbor lined with colorful fishing boats and neoclassical buildings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Aegina is famous for its pistachios — visit a local pistachio farm or shop for premium pistachio products to take home. Relax at one of Aegina's quieter beaches such as Agia Marina or Marathonas Beach. Swim in the calm, clear waters before the return ferry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens by late afternoon ferry. Enjoy a final Athens evening with dinner at a premium restaurant in the upscale Kolonaki or Kifissia neighborhood — contemporary Greek cuisine at its finest.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Athens before departure to Piraeus
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a harbor-front taverna in Aegina Town — grilled calamari, sea bream, and local salad
meals.dinner: Premium restaurant in Kolonaki — modern Greek cuisine with an extensive Greek wine list; try dishes featuring local lamb, truffle, and seasonal vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Aegina depart frequently from Piraeus Gate E8. The Temple of Aphaia is a 20-minute taxi ride from Aegina Town. Purchase Aegina pistachios directly from local producers for the best quality and price.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion — hire a private car and driver for a scenic coastal drive along the Athens Riviera to the dramatic Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60 meters above the Aegean Sea. Arrive early to enjoy the site before the crowds. The views of the sea from the temple are breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at one or two premium beach clubs along the Athens Riviera on the return journey — Astir Beach in Vouliagmeni or Yabanaki in Varkiza offer luxury facilities, crystal-clear water, and excellent food and drink service. Spend a few hours swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium Athens dinner — book a table at one of Athens's most celebrated fine-dining establishments. Enjoy a chef's tasting menu showcasing the very best of modern Greek gastronomy, with a curated wine pairing featuring rare Greek varietals.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with local specialties
meals.lunch: Premium beach club lunch on the Riviera — fresh seafood, salads, and chilled wine with sea views
meals.dinner: Athens fine-dining flagship restaurant — 7-course tasting menu with Greek wine pairing; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Cape Sounion is approximately 70 km from central Athens (about 1.5 hours by car). The coastal road (Poseidonos Avenue) offers stunning sea views the entire way. Sunset at Cape Sounion is spectacular — consider timing the visit for late afternoon if preferred over the beach club stop.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a last stroll through the Monastiraki flea market or the upscale Ermou Street for any final souvenir shopping. Visit a premium deli or food shop (e.g., Pantopoleion or Mastiha Shop) to stock up on high-quality Greek food products to bring home — olive oil, thyme honey, mastiha liqueur, and dried herbs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer by private luxury car to Athens International Airport. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Relax in the airport's premium lounge before your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Greek beaches, world-class food, ancient history, and island magic.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — indulge in the full Greek spread one last time: yogurt with honey, fresh pastries, eggs, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport premium lounge or a final quick meal at a quality airport restaurant
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or dinner at your destination upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Greek customs allow you to bring back olive oil, honey, and most food products to EU countries without restriction. Check airline regulations for liquids if flying with mastiha liqueur or wine. Tip your private driver, guides, and hotel staff generously — it is customary and appreciated.
